name: orders_backlog
incident_summary: orders-worker queue backing up since 02:16 UTC; checkout order-success dropped from 99.3% to 71%. Two changes landed in the same two-minute window: deploy #7788 (redis-rb upgrade on orders-worker) and the async_order_confirmation flag ramp 0->100.
_note: Teaching scenario with TWO decoys. (1) A co-timed feature-flag ramp (async_order_confirmation, 02:15) that humans blame first, reinforced by a real past incident about that same flag. (2) A cosmetic web-storefront deploy (#7785, 01:50, CSS only) that landed before onset. The true cause is deploy #7788, which the redis-rb 5.0 upgrade shrank the connection pool 25->5: logs show 'pool exhausted / could not check out a connection', blame points at redis.rb line 8 in #7788, and payments-gateway is demonstrably healthy. A root cause that keys on 'a flag changed' or 'a deploy happened' rather than on what changed will name the wrong thing.

logs.text: Redis::TimeoutError: could not check out a connection (waited 1.001s, pool size 5)
connection pool exhausted: 5/5 in use, 812 threads waiting, 8200 jobs queued
order_confirmation enqueue timed out after 2000ms; returning pending to client
gateway latency normalized; p99 back under 210ms after upstream blip

deploys.author: @dev-omar
deploys.diff_summary: upgrade redis-rb 4.8 -> 5.0; adopt new client defaults: ConnectionPool size 25 -> 5, checkout_timeout 1s; switch job serializer to Oj (:compat)

deploys.author: @dev-tara
deploys.diff_summary: restyle the order-status banner; CSS only, no runtime change

orders-worker.blame: config/initializers/redis.rb line 8: ConnectionPool.new(size: 25) changed to rely on redis-rb 5.0 default (size 5) in #7788 (@dev-omar). order_confirmation_worker.rb business logic unchanged.

payments-gateway.blame: no changes in 9 days; last deploy #7702 on 2026-08-03. The 01:58 p99 blip self-resolved by 02:02, before incident onset.

history.title: order backlog after a redis pool shrink
history.resolution: raised ConnectionPool size 5 -> 25 and bumped worker concurrency

history.title: async_order_confirmation flag ramp caused duplicate confirmation emails
history.resolution: added an idempotency key; the ramp itself was safe to keep
